title: Cap. VI Arg. 7: Lessius — complete predestination rare in Scripture; hangs on perseverance
pass_a_gloss: And among recent Jesuits Lessius, who more openly pleaded this cause, confidently asserts that of complete predestination there is no mention, or rare mention, in the Scriptures, because this does not hang from the bare good pleasure of God, but from human perseverance. Moreover he teaches that God's intention concerning the number of those to be saved was not absolute before the foresight of the end of the world.
pass_b_english: Among recent Jesuits, Lessius presses it more openly: Scripture barely mentions complete predestination, he says, because it hangs not on bare good pleasure but on human perseverance. He even teaches that God's intention for the number of the saved was not absolute before foresight of the world's end.
source_text: Atque ex nuperis Jesuitis Lessius, qui magis aperte hanc causam egit, confidenter asserit, De completa praedestinatione nullam aut raram esse mentionem in Scripturis, quia haec non pendet ex nudo Dei beneplacito, sed ex perseverantia humana. Quinetiam docet, Intentionem Dei de numero salvandorum non fuisse absolutam ante praevisionem finis mundi.
